提琴是中國傳統的二弦拉弦樂器，屬於胡琴家族。其起源可追溯到新疆及中亞地區，通過絲: The tiqin is a traditional Chinese two-string bowed instrument of the huqin family. Its origin can be traced to Xinjiang and Central Asia, and it came into the Central Plains through cultural exchange along the Silk Road. During the Tang and Song it gradually became part of Han Chinese musical culture, and over several hundred years of improvement and innovation it produced many local styles. By the Ming and Qing it had become an important instrument of folk music and opera accompaniment, widely used in traditional performing arts such as Peking opera and kunqu. Its distinctive timbre can carry a high, piercing line and also a low, sinuous melody, and it is highly expressive. The tiqin is not only found all over China but has travelled with Chinese emigrants around the world, becoming an important vehicle for passing on Chinese culture, and it still holds an important place in contemporary Chinese music.
提琴為中國弦鳴樂器，來源僅載粵樂竹提琴之材質：琴頸以硬木製成，常用酸枝或紫檀；共: The tiqin is a Chinese chordophone, and the source states materials only for the bamboo tiqin of Cantonese music: the neck is of hardwood, usually suanzhi rosewood or red sandalwood; the resonator is a section of large bamboo, its back the natural joint of the bamboo nodes with a soundhole cut in it; the top is not snakeskin but paulownia or palm wood. The name also occasionally refers to the sihu, but the source does not describe its materials; nor does it record the strings, bow stick or bow hair.
提琴音色高亢明亮，具有穿透力強的特點，能在樂隊中清晰突出。其音域寬廣，從低音區的: The tiqin has a high, bright timbre with strong carrying power, and it stands out clearly in an ensemble. Its range is wide, from a warm, full low register to a sharp, exciting top, a broad span with rich expression. The tiqin resonates mainly through the air inside the resonator: the vibration made by the friction of string and bow passes through the bridge into the body and produces a distinctive harmonic pattern. Beside the erhu its timbre is more open and bright; beside the violin it has more of the warm quality of eastern folk character. The tiqin is good at passionate melodies, and its tone can be both gentle and sinuous and high and excited, which makes it an important melodic instrument in Chinese folk orchestras.
提琴（Tiqin）是中國弓弦樂器的名稱，指胡琴家族中數種二弦樂器，以弓拉奏。常見: The tiqin is a name for Chinese bowed instruments, referring to several two-string instruments of the huqin family played with a bow. Common uses include those in kunqu, Cantonese music, and the types used in Fujian and Taiwan, and the name was also once an old term for the sihu. The bamboo tiqin of Cantonese music belongs to the hard-bow line-up of Cantonese opera: the neck is usually hardwood, the soundbox a large section of bamboo, the top of paulownia or palm wood, and the back keeps the bamboo nodes with a soundhole cut in it. The name is also occasionally used loosely for the violin, viola, cello and double bass of the violin family.
